chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Muhammad ibn Qays who said:

I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying, and he was narrating to the people in Makkah: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) prayed the Fajr prayer, then sat with his companions until the sun emerged. So the man after the man arose until there did not remain with him anyone except for two men, one from the Helpers and one from Saqeeff. So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to them both: 'I know that there is a need for the two of you that you would like to ask about it. So if you two want I can inform both of you before you even ask me, and if you want you can both ask me yourselves about it'. They both said, 'But, inform us before we ask you about it, for that is more clarifying for the blindness, and more remote from the doubts, and more affirming for the faith'.

So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'As for you, O brother of Saqeeff, so you came over to ask me about your Ablution and your Prayer, what there is for you regarding that from the goodness. As for your Ablution, so you, when you place your hand into your container, then you say, 'In the Name of Allah', there scatter from it what you accumulated from the sins. So when you wash your face, the sins which your eyes had accumulated with their looks, scatter away from you and are lost. So when you wash your arms, the sins which your right hand and your left hand had accumulated, scatter away from you. So when you wipe your head and your feet, the sins which you walked towards upon your feet scatter away from you. So this is for you from your Ablution'.
ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual benefits of each step of Wudu according to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family)?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated by Imam al-Sadiq (AS) in Mecca, highlights the Prophet’s knowledge of the unspoken intentions of his companions, specifically addressing the Thaqifi man’s inquiry into the spiritual mechanics of ablution. It elucidates the Shia understanding of Wudu as a means of expiating sins committed by specific body parts—eyes, hands, and feet—thereby linking physical purification with moral accountability. The emphasis on 'clearer for the blind' underscores the didactic nature of the Prophet’s teaching, reinforcing the tangible spiritual rewards of ritual acts in Shia jurisprudence.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Muhammad Bin Qays who said,

‘I heard Abu Ja’farasws saying, and heasws was narrating to the people in Makkah: ‘Rasool-Allahsaww prayed the Fajr Salaat, then sat along with hissaww companions until the sun emerged. So the man after the man arose until there did not remain with himsaww anyone except for two man, one from the ‘Helpers’ and one from ‘Saqeef’. So Rasool-Allahsaww said to them both: ‘Isaww know that there is a need for the two of you that you would like to ask about it. So if you two want Isaww can inform both of you before you even ask mesaww, and if you want you can both ask me yourselves about it’. They both said, ‘But, inform us before we ask you about it, for that is more clarifying for the blindness, and more remote from the doubts, and more affirming for the faith’.

Rasool-Allahsaww said: ‘As for you, O brother of Saqeef, so you came over to ask mesaww about your Ablution (Wudhu) and your Salaat, what there is for you regarding that from the goodness. As for your Ablution (Wudhu), so you, when you place your hand into your container, then you say, ‘In the Name of Allahazwj’, there scatter from it what you accumulated from the sins. So when you wash your face, the sins which your eyes had accumulated with their looks, scatter away from you and are lost. So when you wash your arms, the sins which your right hand and your left hand had accumulated, scatter away from you. So when you wipe your head and your feet, the sins which you walked towards upon your feet scatter away from you. So this is for you from your Ablution (Wudhu)’.
en.sarwar: 7. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Mahbub from ibn Ri’ab from Muhammad ibn Qays who has said the following: “I heard abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, say while speaking to people in Makkah, ‘One day the Messenger of Allah completed his Salah (prayer) of the morning and sat in the Masjid with his companions until sunrise.

Thereafter, people one by one left the Masjid except two men, one from the people of Ansar and the other from Thaqif. The Messenger of Allah then said to them, “I understand you need to ask me questions. You may ask if you like and I will answer. If you like, I can tell you what your questions are before you ask. If you wish, you may ask me.” They said, “Please inform us before we ask you our questions; it is more enlightening, frees us from doubts and strengthens our belief more.”

The Messenger of Allah then said, “You, gentleman from Thaqif, have come to ask me about your Wudu’ and Salah (prayer) regarding what is good for you in them. You should keep in mind that when you place your hand in your water container and say ‘In the name of Allah’ the sins that your hands may have committed scatter away from you. The sins that your eyes and mouth may have committed scatter away from you when you wash your face. When you wash your arms to your elbows, the sins from your left and right scatter away from you. When you wipe your head and feet the sins into which you may have walked scatter away from you. This is what you gain from your Wudu’.’””
